chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
You raise your hands at the opening of the prayer opposite your face, and do not raise them all the way.
ai.seo_question: How high should one raise their hands during the opening takbir of prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, clarifies the specific posture of raf' al-yadayn by limiting the hand elevation to the level of the face rather than the ears or head, a detail that distinguishes it from other juristic opinions. It underscores the precision required in the physical acts of worship as derived from the Imams, ensuring the prayer is performed with both humility and adherence to the Prophetic tradition as interpreted by the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘Raise your hands during the opening of the Salāt opposite your face but do not raise them all the way’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
Raise your hands when commencing Salah (prayer) on the sides of your face and do not raise them all the way farther.’”
